lines: i posted the punchline, now waiting for air,
i refresh my feed all around my lair.
maybe they're just slow, i still see it grin,
so i'll share it again, try to begin.
you left the kettle on high next to the pot,
now water's spilling out of the gasket spot.
steam fills your kitchen and drowns the whole room,
you grab a towel, not the actual broom.

topic: seeing the same faces at church
lines: they sit in pews like they've never missed a time,
reciting hymns as if written to a rhyme.
but their lives are still spinning, full of no real plan
just church shoes and smiles from a familiar man.
you still know the code to my private joke code,
we haven't been down that old memory road.
your face lights up just like it did back then,
and for a moment, we're home again.
i watch my goldfish trace the same old tank,
their tiny fins have never yet let them bank
a life beyond these walls i can't ignore
i'd open this glass if i had the right door.
you press the button and it starts to play,
the needle cracks through time's slow decay.
the record spins but you're standing still,
lost in the echoes no one can fill.

topic: seeing your name in a comment
lines: they tagged your name in some random old post,
a meme or a typo, but you read it the most.
you smile at the memories from way back, so old,
and for a second, you feel like you're made of gold.
you think this is some relaxing little tale?
just watch how fast your optimism turns pale.
that goldfish of yours is swimming in spin,
going nowhere fast in its tiny little tin.
you call this a grocery store find? what a deal,
the can's been crushed by a rogue shopping steel.
it's stuck in your cupboard, a sad case of waste,
no one dares ask what the inside might taste.
i press the button to rewind the skip,
remembering how we danced the trip.
i let the tape run out to hear it play,
hoping somehow it still sounds like today.
you ducked past the bouncer and slipped through the gate,
still half-deciding if it was worth the debate.
the music hits your pulse before you see the lights,
the crowd vaults the barriers in time with the nights.
she laughs out loud at the worst puns in tone,
her smile cracks wide even when it's not her own.
her whole face glows like a shy sun, half-erase,
and for once, you believe she belongs in this place.
she scaled the fence and made it past the gate,
but spent ten minutes on the name debate.
security had no clue what to do,
she'd brought a fake id just for you.
your joints whisper warnings as you rise with an ache,
the coffee brews bitter, no time left to make.
you move like a clock losing seconds each slow,
the morning feels older than your body will grow.

topic: reposting a joke that fell flat
lines: she posted the same joke again, another try,
but still got just silence and a few quick reply.
now she sits there, just watching the scroll,
each unread mark takes a new mental toll.
she watches the steam as it makes soft moves,
curling up slowly in lazy grooves.
there's heat in her hands and something in core,
a memory tapping against the door.
she tries on the coat but says it won't wear,
the collar keeps slipping into her hair.
she swears every size makes her feel unfit,
until one is just the right bit.
she blows on the puffball, sets her mind blew,
a hundred white dreams bloom into something new.
they spin through the air with a slow, soft sky,
each seed holds a wish floating miles up so high.
i never wanted our styles to clash,
so i match my jeans with your denim dash.
it wasn't part of my morning plan,
but now you're my favorite outfit fan.
the tag said "thirty" but now you're on sale,
the cashier shrugs when you tell your sad tale.
you argue about the final cost and tax,
she smirks as she dabs her fresh lip balm wax.

topic: reposting a joke that fell flat
lines: he posted the joke, the silence hit the floor,
some laughed but most just rolled their eyes and tore.
he's chasing online clout and viral fame,
though no one will remember his face or name.
the wind came softly and it all blew,
the seeds that meant to stay now fly from you.
they drift up high, a wish for the sky,
and i let them go with a quiet goodbye.
i asked for one degree, not the whole room,
you waved the remote like a messy old broom.
we keep turning it down for a colder chill,
but neither of us wins this small, cold will.
my phone greets strangers but never sees me,
it locks me out every time i use my key.
the camera just stares, no good at the scan,
i swipe past the ai like a regular man.
she slows her pace to fix the left shoe trail,
her breath a whisper, soft and slightly frail.
her hands are steady tying every lace,
but tears fall quiet on her windblown face.
you never said a word, but it sure was a thought,
like you'd planned it ahead or maybe just bought.
we're not trying too hard to look like we seem,
but somehow it feels like a match made in dream.
you swear the room feels colder than a snowstorm's chill,
i check the vents - we're fine, but you still want to fill
the silence with your sighs and turning it down,
as if frost would form at your icy little crown.
you boost over the bouncer and the gate,
depending on luck and sheer fate.
the ticket is lost, but your smile feels fake,
so you hide in the crowd, trying not to break.
i saw my left shoe begin to untie its lace,
i grinned and kept going - this might be my race.
these sneakers have never once asked me to stay,
just sprint with me forward as bold as they.
i build whole battles out of tiny fights,
the action figures pose in stage lights.
they never speak but they live their role,
and every move feels like it's from the soul.
you stare at your screen, still not ready to post,
the perfect words slip away from the host.
you rephrase and delete, but it's all just a try,
your humor feels rusty, your wit feels so dry.
you never learned the way my name should say,
you blur it, let it fall just like that away.
i've spelled it out for you three times by now, through,
but in your head, it's still some other hue.

topic: reposting a joke that fell flat
lines: i posted the joke again - same tired try,
my humor still hits the room and feels dry.
the chat sits quiet, no laugh from the bar,
not even a cringe-worthy attempt at a star.
they looked you up, but they didn't see the scene,
your face just slipped off their phone-screen routine.
you said your name, but they clearly haven't tried,
so you sigh and accept how they've left you denied.
you slip through the fence like some masterful gate,
your confidence built on bad luck and fate.
you miss every lyric, of course there's a lack,
but you act so amazed when they turn to look back.
she leaned down softly and blew them all blew,
swore she could see each tiny wish turn true.
they spiraled through air, defying the sky,
"why can't dreams last as long as seeds do?" she'd sigh.
i watched it drift in your old fish tank,
slow circles where your childhood had sank.
it swam toward the top like the sky was below,
and i wondered aloud, "why must it be so?"
i wore my sweater that's loud and pink,
you asked if it went with your new red drink.
we laughed about trying to be a match,
but even mismatched we still fix the patch.
she's been chasing that goal all along the trail,
but the laces keep coming loose and she won't fail.
she bends down and reties that stubborn knot,
picks up pace - she already knew what she'd got.
she paused mid-stride where the path made a trail,
afraid the whole run was about to fail.
her fingers tightened around the loose lace,
her breath still warm on the morning's cold face.
i raised my hand and asked what it would say,
he said, "no names, no dates - no grades this way."
i turned the paper back with a guilty grin,
but now i can't read anything i've written in.

topic: laughing too hard at a joke
lines: you laugh until it turns into a full-on fit,
your sides ache where the joy just hits it.
you chase the moment, won't let it stay away,
because some laughs feel like a gift today.
she calls him by the wrong names,
catching herself mid-sentence, mid-frames.
he laughs and says "it's okay, you can smile,"
and they both forget why they were frowning awhile.
she watches the steam curl into a slow twist,
reads every message she missed in the list.
her tea goes cold while she holds back from pour,
fingers tapping send but there's nothing more.
you notice your lace as you pick up pace,
the trail blurs by, but you keep the race.
you stop at the bend to finally tie
one sneaker, then laugh at the blue sky.
it keeps going clockwise, around and again,
like some tiny, liquid, gold-tinted chain.
it treads water, spins, repeats its tight spin,
you'd think after years, it would quit its thin skin.
you knit in the quiet, a slow-moving hush,
the yarn holds your warmth in a gentle blush.
your fingers move sure as they trace the thread,
i fall into rhythm, right where you lead.
i try to wear it, but it still doesn't fit,
the fabric clings where the armpits should sit.
i hang it up, just out of reach from self,
maybe tomorrow it'll be the right shelf.
i open the fridge and my stomach fills with fear,
something's off, something is visibly near.
i reach for the can but i hesitate to twist,
maybe it passed its date or i just plain missed.
you survived a storm and came out with a scar,
the dent on your tin marks where it hit the car.
now you stand there proud, like a king's old crown,
holding what it takes to feed the whole town.
you slipped past security through an open gate,
no line, no tickets, no need to wait.
your whole escape was genius from the plan,
now you're front row, the crowd's your fan.
you watch the bees drift where the petals turn gold,
their wings too light to hold what they're told.
the blossom-lit path stretches toward the sky,
but the wind will not let beauty quietly die.
i watched the dandelion seeds fly through the sky,
they drifted slowly, floating way up high.
i felt so calm once i was truly done,
the breeze caught them all, spun them toward the sun.
her left shoe comes loose at the double knot,
she slows to a walk where the path turns to spot.
she counts every step as a wasted mile,
the run now feels more like a solo trial.
your face won't load - the system fails your scan,
you tap the screen again and again, no man.
you fumble through seven wrong codes to unlock,
your phone just stares like a cold, dead rock.
i remember every step, every moves,
still feeling the beat in my old grooves.
back then, we danced through the summer nights,
now it's just screens and dim computer lights.
she wakes to a body that sounds like a creak,
probably slept weird all last week.
she stares at the pillow, now tangled and still,
then stretches like a willow in a stiff chill.
she turns on the kettle to bring water to boil,
her hands shake a bit from the chill of the soil.
steam curls upward as she begins to pour,
the tea's not enough - she wants something more.
it plays in my head like some endless loop,
the whole office watches me dance in a group.
they ask if i missed a single flaw,
but i hit every step - this is dance law.
they found a goldfish floating belly-up below,
its scales still shimmer with a sickly glow.
she tries to flip it gently with a chopstick grip,
but nothing moves - it's frozen in that flip.
you smile and nod, pretend it all comes again,
but your brain skips the rhythm, the flow, the refrain.
you sip your drink and you hope it will fold
your guilt into silence with stories of old.
she mutters about the dust in this room,
how every shadow looks like a broom.
the needles click once, click twice, click again,
but the noise is too much for her fragile brain.
you still laugh at every joke we told
when we were too young to be self-aware and bold.
i see you smile as your eyes glance at the wave,
remembering moments that only we called brave.

topic: someone spilling punch on the rug
lines: you watched the punch spread out like a red rose,
but then you grabbed the bucket, the sponge, the hose.
the rug is still wet, but we made it look new
and maybe this mess just reminded us of you.
you've been waiting for steam to rise from your wait,
but the tea sits cold on your dinner plate.
the kettle hums low, it refuses to grow,
you really should buy a new one, you know.
she waits for the breeze to carry them blow,
each fluff a new life yet to grow.
they twirl in the sky on an upward air,
she watches with pride, not a single one spare.

topic: seeing the same faces at church
lines: he still calls them by the old names,
though their hair's gone gray and eyes lost their flames.
he's been counting these same faces for years,
not realizing they're ghosts now, not cheers.
you kept running even when that sneaker's lace
started to drag and you lost your race.
you didn't slow down or let it be a trip,
just ran with the pain and refused to slip.
you twist and push but nothing seems to try,
your hands are shaking, stressed and going dry.
the outlet glares, the plug won't make it fit,
you almost scream, "this nonsense just won't quit."
my laugh was loud though no one heard the joke,
i'm pretty sure my face might have broke.
i sat there sweating on the inside edge,
like a smile forced into a tight wedge.
she lets them go like wishes in flight,
each tiny puff catching morning's light.
they spin toward some distant land,
she opens hers - ready to stand.
you thought you heard your name in that sound,
but it's just steam going up all around.
it's hissing like a tiny cloud,
you yell "i'm coming!" out loud.
the needles move fast, but the rhythm feels soft,
my thoughts drift aloft where the sky meets the loft.
i tuck in each stitch, then i smooth out the fold,
the room stays so cold, but my hands stay bold.
i can't focus - my mind won't find rest,
it's been hours since my thoughts left their nest.
my hands follow the rhythm of the thread,
while silence grows from something into dread.
she laughs too long, she leans right in,
her smile is bright but burning like a din.
they all talk over her, they speak so loud,
she leaves just when she isn't proud.

topic: seeing a price tag too high
lines: your eyes hit the price tag and register shock,
while time ticks on like a slow-moving clock.
you whisper, "this was never my true fate,"
then walk out, still carrying the item's weight.
i wait for the kettle to start to sing,
it whistles like something not quite a thing.
i pour the hot water fast into my brew,
but now my new socks are half a stew.
the teacher dropped the test like it was a fail,
your name still on it like an old, faint trail.
you trace the red marks made in quick, dry ink,
wondering if this is the edge or the brink.
